events.title: Frederick II is crowned emperor
events.shortBlurb: In St. Peter's, Pope Honorius III set the imperial crown on his former ward, who vowed a crusade and swore to guard the Church…
body: Frederick II of Hohenstaufen, king of Sicily through his Norman mother and king of Germany through his father Henry VI, had as a fatherless boy been the ward of Pope Innocent III. His old tutor, Cencio Savelli, now reigned as Pope Honorius III and had labored to bring him peacefully to the imperial dignity.

On 22 November 1220 Honorius crowned Frederick Holy Roman Emperor in St. Peter's Basilica at Rome. During the ceremony Frederick took the cross once more, renewing his vow to lead a crusade to the Holy Land, and at the pope's request he promulgated constitutions protecting the rights of the Church and clergy and issued severe edicts against heretics, placing the secular sword at the service of the faith.

The concord did not endure. Frederick's repeated postponement of his crusade and his ambition to rule all Italy would bring him into a long duel with the papacy, and he was excommunicated under Gregory IX and again under Innocent IV, who at Lyons in 1245 declared him deposed. But on this day pope and emperor stood together in seeming amity in the basilica of the Apostle.
